title: Strategic Technical Debt: A Real Options Approach to Early-Stage Software Experimentation
abstract: arXiv:2608.16112v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Technical debt is treated almost universally as an engineering pathology. This paper argues that under the conditions defining early-stage software work (high hypothesis uncertainty, cheap experiments, and the freedom to abandon), deliberately incurred technical debt is a rationally priced financial instrument: a call option on the validated product, purchased at a discount that is largest exactly when uncertainty is highest. We make three contributions. First, a demarcation: debt is strategic when its expected cost loads on the success branch of the venture (repaid only if the hypothesis validates) and toxic when it imposes unconditional cost while held (security exposure, data loss, corrupted experimental signal), a boundary stated formally that renders the popular "prudent vs. reckless" intuition testable. tldr: 本文提出战略性技术债务是一种实物期权，在早期软件实验的高不确定性下，它可作为合理定价的金融工具，并提供了区分战略性与有害债务的正式边界及动态模型。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes that strategic technical debt is a real option, rationally priced under high uncertainty in early-stage software experimentation, and provides a formal boundary distinguishing strategic from toxic debt along with a dynamic model.
